metadata.title: Pentagon brings on Grok and ChatGPT for military use

sources.news_title: Pentagon Adds Grok And ChatGPT To Military AI Platform
sources.text:
The Pentagon has added OpenAI's ChatGPT and xAI's Grok for Government to its enterprise generative AI platform, expanding the artificial intelligence tools available to Defense Department personnel.
The models will be offered through GenAI.mil, a platform launched last year to give Defense Department employees access to commercial AI systems. The platform initially offered Google's Gemini for Government and now has more than 1.7 million users.
ChatGPT Mil will focus on document-heavy, unclassified work such as planning, policy, logistics and administration. The Defense Department says it is designed to support more than 3 million personnel.
The expansion comes amid the Pentagon's broader effort to incorporate commercial AI into military operations. OpenAI and xAI have also secured agreements to provide models for classified environments.

sources.news_title: ChatGPT Mil Goes Live Across The War Department
sources.text:
The War Department launched OpenAI’s ChatGPT Mil on GenAI.mil Monday, adding a secure version of ChatGPT designed to support more than 3 million military and civilian personnel.
The department said the system has accreditation for Controlled Unclassified Information at Impact Level 5 and supports document-heavy unclassified work involving planning, policy, logistics and administration.
The launch advances an enterprise partnership between the War Department and OpenAI that began in 2025. The Dallas Express previously reported in February that the department planned to bring ChatGPT to GenAI.mil after the platform reached one million users.
ChatGPT Mil goes live
ChatGPT Mil centers on chat, files, projects and custom GPTs, with additional features planned over time, according to the department.
OpenAI said in its February announcement that the customized system runs in authorized government cloud infrastructure. OpenAI keeps data processed through GenAI.mil isolated from its public and commercial models and does not use the data to train or improve those models, according to the company.
The company said the system can help personnel summarize policy and guidance documents, draft and review procurement materials, generate internal reports and compliance checklists, and support research, planning and administrative workflows.
Military expands AI options
The ChatGPT Mil rollout is part of a broader push to give personnel access to multiple frontier AI systems. The War Department also launched Starshield AI’s Grok for Government on GenAI.mil Monday.
The department said GenAI.mil has onboarded more than 1.7 million unique users since its launch nine months ago. Officials said using multiple models reduces dependence on a single vendor while expanding AI tools across the Joint Force.
The Chief Digital and AI Office and the Office of the Under Secretary of War for Research and Engineering will continue expanding the department’s frontier AI capabilities. Officials said the ChatGPT Mil launch also supports the White House AI Action Plan and the department’s effort to use AI for military missions and decision-making.

sources.news_title: Grok and ChatGPT join Gemini in Pentagon’s enterprise genAI portal
sources.text:
Grok and ChatGPT join Gemini in Pentagon’s enterprise genAI portal
The Pentagon’s suite of commercial generative AI products has expanded beyond Google’s Gemini offering, according to officials who told DefenseScoop Monday that insiders can now chat with approved versions of OpenAI’s ChatGPT and Starshield AI’s Grok frontier models when they log on to the GenAI.mil platform.
This long-anticipated integration is intended to enable U.S. personnel to apply the distinct technical strengths of each top-tier large language model provider to meet specialized military missions.
“Access to a diverse suite of AI capabilities from across the resilient American technology stack will give warfighters the tools they need to act with confidence and safeguard the nation against any threat,” said a source who asked to be referred to as a War Department official.
(Officially changing the Defense Department’s name requires an act of Congress, but last year President Donald Trump signed an executive order rebranding DOD as the Department of War.)
Frontier AI encompasses the most advanced, large-scale, and capable foundational models that are pushing the boundaries of machine intelligence.
Within that realm is the emerging field of generative AI and associated large language models, which broadly produce convincing but not always correct text, software code, images, audio and other media from human prompts.
Commercial genAI products have maintained much hype since they were released to the general public in late 2022. However, experts have increasingly warned of severe known and unknown threats that the conversational tech poses to humanity, privacy, public trust, democratic processes and military operations.
In December 2025, the DOD unveiled plans for a swift and expansive release of the GenAI.mil platform to unleash advanced AI models to more than 3 million military members, civilian employees and contractors. Google Cloud’s Gemini for Government products were the first to go live in the one-stop shop. Officials at the time said that other models — including Anthropic’s Claude, OpenAI’s ChatGPT and xAI’s Grok — would soon follow.
However, a dispute between the Pentagon and Anthropic derailed plans to add Claude to the platform. The company’s leadership insisted on stricter contractual guardrails that would prevent DOD from applying the firm’s AI technology to conduct mass surveillance of Americans or be used in connection to lethal autonomous weapons. The Pentagon, in turn, demanded unrestricted access to deploy any genAI products it purchased for what its leaders deem to be “lawful purposes.”
About six months ago, the department formally designated Anthropic a “supply-chain risk” and ordered personnel to purge the company’s AI products from all national security systems and assets. The Claude maker subsequently sued the government, and last week a federal district judge ruled that the Pentagon’s designation and actions against Anthropic were “illegal and baseless.”
“The Department of War will continue to build an architecture that prevents AI vendor lock and ensures long-term flexibility for the Joint Force,” the source who asked to be referred to as a War Department official said in response to questions from DefenseScoop Monday about the latest GenAI.mil announcements.
DOD uses an “Impact Level” classification system to ensure that cloud-based data hosting environments and services are safe and compliant with existing policies.
The department’s press releases about Grok and ChatGPT joining Gemini on GenAI.mil indicate that each of the industry-leading frontier models have cleared Impact Level 5, or IL5, which covers the highest authorization granted to environments built to store and process non-public, sensitive unclassified data.
“We are moving at wartime speed: empowering the department to experiment, iterate, and deploy capabilities faster than our adversaries can adapt,” the War Department official said.
DOD’s initial announcement Monday revealed that OpenAI’s ChatGPT Mil “brings a familiar commercial experience” into the secure GenAI.mil environment that’s “tailored to warfighter needs.” In particular, the product will support document-heavy unclassified pursuits around planning, policy, logistics, and administration.
“The core experience centers on chat, files, projects, and custom GPTs, with additional features sequenced over time,” Pentagon officials wrote in the press release.
A person familiar with the work at OpenAI said that DOD employees can now use ChatGPT Mil to generate reliable models for repeatable workflows — like filling out travel forms or responding to contracting opportunities.
“Personnel will soon be able to chat directly with GPT-5.6 Terra, OpenAI’s latest frontier model, bringing our most advanced model to research, analysis, drafting, and other day-to-day work,” the source told DefenseScoop, noting that the prior version 5.4 Terra is currently offered.
ChatGPT Mil also organizes relevant files and conversations that occur over months-long projects in one place, they added, as well as an “Offline Search capability” that provides detailed citations and can be refreshed to reflect new information as it emerges.
“This integration is grounded in our national security principles, pairing access to powerful tools with clear safeguards, meaningful human judgment, and accountability for high-stakes decisions,” Joe Larson, a former senior Pentagon official who now serves as OpenAI’s vice president and head of government, said in a statement.
Meanwhile, billionaire Elon Musk rebranded and merged his companies xAI and SpaceX into a combined corporate powerhouse earlier this year.
Starshield AI’s Grok for Government is an xAI Grok frontier model that’s tailored for federal use.
Per DOD’s announcement, Grok for Government will supply personnel with “advanced capabilities, including deep-thinking inference, adaptive reasoning modes (Auto, Fast, and Expert), customizable workspaces, persistent projects and reusable ‘playbooks’ that capture and scale institutional knowledge” via GenAI.mil.
Spokespersons from xAI and SpaceX did not respond to requests for comment on Monday.

sources.news_title: The Pentagon now has its own version of ChatGPT and Grok
sources.text:
The Pentagon has launched versions of OpenAI’s ChatGPT and xAI’s Grok, giving 3 million civilian and military personnel access to generative AI tools that have been tailored to “warfighter needs.”
ChatGPT Mil and Grok for Government — custom versions of the popular consumer generative AI tools — are now part of GenAI.mil, a centralized, secure portal launched last year.
GenAI.mil, which offered Google Gemini when it first launched, is designed to give Department of Defense employees access to commercial frontier AI models without sending sensitive government data through ordinary consumer channels. In particular, the official military version is exempt from the data collection that is difficult to avoid in consumer tech products.
And according to the Department of Defense, the generative AI portal has proven popular. GenAI.mil has already onboarded more than 1.7 million unique users out of the department’s 3 million personnel, according to the department.
These latest additions are part of the Pentagon’s broader effort to use AI tools to accelerate work and give the Department of Defense an edge without sacrificing security. They also highlight the absence of Anthropic’s Claude model and the Pentagon’s effort to work with other companies following its dispute with the frontier lab. Anthropic was labeled a supply-chain risk by the Trump administration — a designation that it is currently fighting in court — after it refused to give the Pentagon unrestricted use of its AI tools and instead insisted on certain safety guardrails.
ChatGPT Mil, which came out of the company’s OpenAI for Government program, will offer an experience familiar to commercial ChatGPT users. The tool will focus on chat, files, projects, and custom GPTs, according to the Defense Department. The tool will also support document-heavy, routine unclassified work such as administrative tasks, logistics, planning, and policy. Other features will be added over time.
The Pentagon positioned Grok’s capabilities and potential uses in much broader and more militaristic terms.
“Starshield AI’s Grok for Government will provide the warfighter with immediate productivity gains, stronger knowledge continuity and more secure and efficient collaboration,” according to the Defense Department’s press release. (SpaceX’s Starshield AI is a secure satellite network that uses the company’s existing Starlink tech.)
The department added that Grok would allow its military “to execute missions faster and with greater precision across numerous operational contexts, ranging from market research analysis for acquisition professionals to supply-chain management for logisticians.”
The Pentagon has struck deals with a number of other tech companies in a bid to boost its AI capabilities, including Amazon Web Services, Microsoft, Nvidia, and Reflection AI.

sources.news_title: Pentagon brings on Grok and ChatGPT for military use
Pentagon Broadens AI Tools to Include ChatGPT and Grok
sources.text:
The Pentagon rolled out OpenAI’s ChatGPT Mil and Starshield AI’s Grok for Government from SpaceX across the military Monday, giving personnel two new commercial AI tools for sensitive, unclassified work.
ChatGPT Mil and Grok for Government are each built for “secure, consistent enterprise use” across a department of more than 3 million military and civilian personnel, the Defense Department said. The tools are available through GenAI.mil, the Pentagon’s internal generative AI platform, which launched in December with Google’s Gemini. More than 1.7 million personnel have used the platform since then,according to the department.
The Pentagon says ChatGPT Mil is designed for “document-heavy unclassified work,” including planning, policy, logistics and administration.
Grok for Government includes multiple reasoning modes, customizable workspaces and reusable “playbooks.” The Pentagon said it can be used across “numerous operational contexts,” including acquisition research and supply-chain management.
Trending
The expansion also comes as the Pentagon faces security concerns over how its workforce uses commercial AI. In June, the Defense Counterintelligence and Security Agency warned that unauthorized “shadow AI” tools could create data leaks and other security risks. Congress has separately ordered the Pentagon to assess cybersecurity risks from authorized and unauthorized AI software.
The rollout deepens the Pentagon’s ties with OpenAI and xAI as the department expands its use of commercial AI and wrestles with how much control companies can keep over military uses of their technology.
That fight came to a head with Anthropic, which resisted Pentagon demands that its Claude models be available for all lawful military uses. Anthropic sought safeguards against mass domestic surveillance and fully autonomous weapons.
The Pentagon designated Anthropic a national security supply-chain risk. A federal judge struck down that designation last week, ruling that the government had unlawfully retaliated against the company.
OpenAI took a different path. The company reached a separate agreement with the Pentagon that allows its models to be used for lawful purposes while maintaining limits on domestic surveillance, autonomous weapons and some high-stakes decisions without human involvement.
OpenAI says it can enforce those limits through contractual and technical safeguards, including keeping control of its safety systems and providing its models through the cloud rather than directly on weapons or other devices.
Monday’s announcement does not say whether those same restrictions apply to ChatGPT Mil. It says the tool can be used for planning but does not specify whether that includes operational or military planning or whether it can be used for intelligence analysis, targeting, weapons-related work or decisions involving the use of force.
Asked about those uses, a Pentagon official said tools on GenAI.mil are certified to handle controlled unclassified information at Impact Level 5 but did not address the specific activities.
In May, the Pentagon announced a separate effort to deploy advanced commercial AI models on classified Impact Level 6 and 7 networks. The department said those systems would support operational uses including data synthesis, situational awareness and warfighter decision-making.

sources.news_title: The military’s ChatGPT is now live via the Pentagon’s GenAI platform
sources.text:
The Pentagon’s secure artificial intelligence platform now has ChatGPT.
The Department of Defense on Monday launched OpenAI’s ChatGPT Mil on GenAI.mil, making the chatbot available for work involving controlled unclassified information, or CUI — sensitive government information that is not classified but still requires specific safeguards.
The department said ChatGPT Mil is accredited for CUI at Impact Level 5, a DoD cloud-security standard for certain sensitive unclassified information.
ChatGPT Mil joins Google Gemini on GenAI.mil, giving military and civilian users access to multiple frontier AI models. A Defense Department official told Defense One that Gemini is useful for search, while ChatGPT can be used for more text-based work, allowing users to select a model for a particular task.
GenAI.mil is becoming a multi-model platform. The Defense Department also launched Starshield AI’s Grok for Government on GenAI.mil on Monday, saying the addition would help eliminate vendor lock-in and promote a broader American AI ecosystem.
GenAI.mil has already attracted more than 1.7 million unique users, according to the Defense Department. The platform launched nine months ago and is intended to serve the department’s more than 3 million personnel.
For the Navy and Marine Corps, GenAI.mil is already an enterprise requirement. A January Navy memorandum designated it as the Department of the Navy’s mandated CUI and IL5 generative-AI platform and directed Navy organizations and commands to transition to it by April 30.
Navy guidance states that GenAI.mil is authorized for CUI but prohibits the use of personally identifiable information and protected health information.
The initial ChatGPT Mil experience includes chat, files, projects and custom GPTs, with additional features expected over time, according to the Defense Department. The platform is designed for document-heavy work including planning, policy, logistics and administration.
An OpenAI official told Defense One potential military uses include disaster-response planning, resource allocation, reconciling supply and maintenance information and drafting transportation requirements.
The Defense Department has already cited a military example of GenAI.mil’s use. In May congressional testimony, the department said the Army’s XVIII Airborne Corps used the platform to produce a complete exercise operations order for the U.S. Southern Command area of responsibility in six weeks, with nine writers producing work that traditionally requires six to nine months by a much larger staff.
Preparing frontier models for GenAI.mil requires security testing involving the Defense Information Systems Agency and National Security Agency, according to a former defense official who spoke to Defense One.
GenAI.mil is an IL5 enterprise platform for unclassified work, not the classified AI capabilities the Defense Department is separately developing and testing for combat operations. Defense One reported that Pentagon and OpenAI officials do not intend to use models on GenAI.mil for combat; the department is developing AI capabilities for classified networks and warfighting missions.
OpenAI’s government sales chief Joe Larson said ChatGPT on GenAI.mil is intended to make unclassified work more efficient while maintaining safeguards, human judgment and accountability for high-stakes decisions.
OpenAI also said data processed on GenAI.mil remains isolated within the government environment and is not used to train or improve its public or commercial models.
Natalie Oliverio is an independent journalist and Navy veteran who covers military and veterans’ issues. Drawing on her experience as a talent executive and mentor, she writes about the policies, people and programs shaping the military community.

sources.news_title: Pentagon launches Musk’s Grok for military use
sources.text:
The War Department launched Grok, SpaceXAI founder Elon Musk’s chatbot, for military use more than a year after signing a contract with Starshield AI.
Starshield AI’s Grok for Government is Musk’s flagship attempt to assist the U.S. government with its adoption of artificial intelligence. A press release from the Pentagon said the initiative would expand “the suite of frontier AI capabilities on GenAI.mil, the Department’s premier generative AI platform.” The AI is “engineered for secure, consistent enterprise use” and accredited for Controlled Unclassified Information at Impact Level 5.
Recommended Stories
“Starshield AI’s Grok for Government will provide the warfighter with immediate productivity gains, stronger knowledge continuity and more secure and efficient collaboration,” the Pentagon press release reads. “By bringing Starshield AI’s Grok to GenAI.mil, Department personnel will gain access to advanced capabilities, including deep-thinking inference, adaptive reasoning modes… customizable workspaces, persistent projects and reusable ‘playbooks’ that capture and scale institutional knowledge.”
The launch will enable the military to “execute missions faster and with greater precision” in areas ranging from market research analysis to supply chain management, according to the release.
Over half of the Pentagon’s 3 million personnel already use GenAI.mil, according to the release, and the department plans to continue to expand the scale of the military’s use of AI.
The initiative was secured last year, when the Pentagon also signed contracts with Anthropic, Google, and OpenAI, with each receiving $200 million.
Musk’s AI company has fared well due to his usually positive relationship with President Donald Trump, unlike the combative relationship he has with Anthropic.
PENTAGON ANNOUNCES IT WILL BEGIN USING GROK, X’S AI
Grok is viewed as one of the most promising AI tools due to its training on X’s data. A problem encountered by AI developers is that engineers have run out of data to plug into AI models to further develop their skills. While other models must spend time and effort creating synthetic data, Grok has a constant inflow of new data to work with through the massive amount of content produced by X users.
Despite its promise, Grok is also one of the most controversial AI models. Last year, a tweak to its code to allow it to make “politically incorrect” statements went awry. Within a day, the chatbot was praising Adolf Hitler, endorsing a new Holocaust, and threatening to sexually assault at least one user. Adjustments since have prevented another incident of equal severity, but it has led to some lasting doubts about its capabilities.

sources.news_title: The US military gets its own ChatGPT today
sources.text:
The US military gets its own ChatGPT today
After months of security testing, Pentagon adds an OpenAI product to the list of AI tools approved for unclassified work.
Updated: 5:29 p.m.
The Pentagon’s main portal for AI tools now offers ChatGPT and Grok for Government alongside Google Gemini.
A Defense Department official said the OpenAI product, dubbed ChatGPT Mil, would bring new strengths to GenAI.mil, where troops and defense civilians can use generative-AI tools to work on controlled, unclassified information, or CUI.
“Gemini, I like for search functionality or scraping certain sources. Chat for more, like, text-based work,” said the official, who requested anonymity to speak before the official announcement on Monday. “We want to have access to all these different models, so people, if they prefer one for a certain task, they can use it.”
Work began in February to create a version of ChatGPT that could be used for CUI. In June, an OpenAI official said they believed it would be deployed in “early July.”
A DOD press release slated for release today said ChatGPT Mil would bring “a familiar commercial experience into the Department’s secure environment, tailored to warfighter needs...ChatGPT Mil supports document-heavy unclassified work across the Department, including planning, policy, logistics, and administration, and is built for scale to support more than 3 million Department personnel. This deployment accelerates routine tasks and frees up time for more critical projects across the Joint Force.”
One OpenAI official, who requested anonymity to speak before the official announcement, offered ideas for how the military might use its special version of ChatGPT. Operators at Northern Command might use it to streamline planning, resource allocation, or disaster response with FEMA or other parts of the federal government. Or the Joint Staff’s logistics directorate might use it to simplify paperwork and documentation. The official also suggested that logisticians at combatant commands “would be a natural audience, with uses such as reconciling supply and maintenance updates, drafting transportation requirements.”
In background talks, OpenAI and Pentagon officials said they don’t want to use models on the GenAI.mil platform for combat. The Pentagon has argued that they should be able to use AI products as they like, a sticking point in disagreements between the department and AI model maker Anthropic. And OpenAI has said that ChatGPT’s need for connectivity and large amounts of computing power doesn’t make it a good fit for combat anyway. The department is continually testing and seeking a number of other tools for those types of operations and actions.
Customized for security
Like the GenAI.mil version of Gemini, the military version of ChatGPT has additional security functions built in.
“When you're dealing with CUI within the department, it's obvious this is stuff that cannot be on a commercial model. We have to build it in a separate sort of environment. So it's engineered in a way to be separate from the commercial model,” said the defense official.
Prepping a frontier model for use on GenAI.mil is an “arduous” process, said one former defense official who was involved in such tests. It requires building out the “environment”—that is, finding the compute resources, keeping track of the users and their unique security conditions, compiling the data that the model will use, and anticipating the sorts of requests that users may have.
“Think of having to pass security guardrails for both DISA [Defense Information Systems Agency] and the NSA,” the former defense official said.
As DISA builds the environment, NSA looks for ways that attackers might invade it—or the model might escape it, the official said.
The Pentagon launched GenAI.mil on Dec. 9 with one tool: Google’s Gemini. Around the same time, Pentagon officials signed an agreement to bring Elon Musk’s xAI tool to the platform, but no formal deployment has since been announced. On Monday, the Pentagon announced that Grok for Government, an AI product of Musk's Starshield AI, was now available on GenAI.mil.
Joe Larson, who leads OpenAI’s government sales, said, “ChatGPT on GenAI.mil will make unclassified work throughout the Department more efficient, freeing up time and resources so DoD personnel can focus on the mission. This integration is grounded in our national security principles, pairing access to powerful tools with clear safeguards, meaningful human judgment, and accountability for high-stakes decisions. We’re excited to see what the Department’s extraordinary workforce builds with it.”
